species: Spinacia oleracea (3JCU photosystem II–LHCII supercomplex); ATP synthase and carriers are not drawn from a single measured assembly

evidence_classes.experimental: Deposited coordinates of photosystem II–LHCII only.
evidence_classes.derived: Orientation (flattest direction of the PSII core subunits = membrane normal) and membrane position (centre of the D1 protein) from stated rules.
evidence_classes.modelled: The compartment model: light response, linear and cyclic electron flow, photosynthetic control, ATP synthesis, leak and Calvin cycle are teaching-level relations with round constants.
evidence_classes.illustrative: Free proton, ATP and NADPH counts, their positions and speeds, and the display time scale.

equations.name: light response
equations.formula: L' = L + (light - L)*min(1, h/0.3); act' = act + (light - act)*min(1, h/6)

equations.name: Calvin cycle
equations.formula: Jcal = 0.12*act*ATP/(ATP+0.3)*NADPH/(NADPH+0.05); ATP uses 3 per cycle, NADPH 2

clocks: Model seconds (teaching time); the model steps on a 0.02 s grid; light switches fade over 0.3 s, Calvin activation over 6 s.
limitations: Constants are teaching values chosen to show light response, cyclic flow, uncoupler and inhibitor behaviour; not fitted to measurements.
Only the PSII–LHCII structure is in the scene; the b6f complex, PSI, ATP synthase and carriers are not drawn from a measured assembly.
The work does not draw electron paths through the real cofactors or proton pumping on the structure (still the classic code).
literature: Structure of spinach photosystem II-LHCII supercomplex at 3.2 A resolution. Nature 2016, doi:10.1038/nature18020
Mitchell P. Chemiosmotic coupling in oxidative and photosynthetic phosphorylation. Biol Rev 1966

validation.note: The data model equals the classic compartment model bit for bit over scripted switch schedules; it is a teaching model, not a fit to measurements, and has not been reviewed by a domain expert.
